fields.name: field_multizone
fields.description: Three crop zones meeting at diagonal boundaries — canola (yellow), wheat/grass (green), bare soil (brown). Strong spatial variation, clear non-axis-aligned zone edges.
fields.notes: Best overall for optimizer demos. pseudo_ndvi separates canola (high) from soil (low) cleanly. Diagonal zone boundaries justify non-zero orientation.

fields.name: field_orchard
fields.description: Orchard or citrus grove with distinct tree canopy rows, tractor visible on access road. Clear diagonal row orientation ~30-40 degrees from horizontal.
fields.notes: Smallest source image — use target_size=32 to avoid upscaling artifacts. Best for orientation_deg demo: rows are clearly not east-west. Green channel cleanly separates canopy from paths.

fields.name: field_elevation
fields.description: Oblique aerial view of multiple adjacent field parcels — vineyard rows on left, broad green fields on right, tree windbreak through centre. Multiple distinct crop types.
fields.notes: Oblique angle compresses geometry but still produces useful priority variation. Use low threshold (0.15) since mean priority is low (0.18). The windbreak trees will appear as a linear high-priority band — interesting edge case.

fields.name: field_meadow
fields.description: Single grass field with mowing/tractor tracks visible, irregular boundary with trees and bushes on all sides. Best candidate for field_mask demo.
fields.notes: The main value here is the irregular boundary — derive a field_mask by thresholding the green channel before passing to generate_strips(). The mow tracks create subtle row-like structure but variation is low overall.

fields.name: field_paddies
fields.description: Flooded rice paddy plots — waterlogged bare soil in rectangular plots, green vegetation borders and trees. Building with blue roof visible top-left.
fields.notes: Invert=True: bare flooded plots have low NDVI (= low priority after inversion means high priority without invert — use invert=False and threshold to keep green edges). Actually keep invert=True so green vegetation edges = high priority spray zones. High threshold (0.4) keeps only the dense green border areas. Shows well how drones would spray field margins and skip flooded centres.
